old: 这套规定 1950 年写入联邦法规（21 CFR 133），软质熟成奶酪一节（133.182）原文就是这一句。
new: 这条规定可追溯到 1949 年联邦政府发布的奶酪身份标准，现行条文收在 21 CFR 第 133 部分，软质熟成奶酪一节（133.182）写得最明白。
why: 两处问题：(1) 年份。联邦奶酪身份标准的终版规则 1949 年 4 月刊登于联邦公报（Knoll 2005 引 14 F.R. 1960）；1950 只见于 Food Safety News 等二手时间线。「可追溯到 1949 年」可辩护，与 hist_A 的 raw60 条一致。(2) 「1950 年写入 21 CFR 133」是时代错置：Part 133 这个编号是 1977 年重编时才有的（133.182 / 133.165 的来源行都是 42 FR 14366, 1977 年 3 月 15 日），此前在 Part 19。另外 133.182 原文是「If the milk used is not pasteurized, the cheese so made is cured at a temperature of not less than 35 °F for not less than 60 days」，页面是转述，不宜说「原文就是这一句」。

new: The rule goes back to the federal cheese standards of identity issued in 1949 and now sits in 21 CFR Part 133; the soft-ripened cheese section (§133.182) spells it out.
why: Same as zh: the standards were published as a final rule in April 1949 (1950 is a secondary-source date), and "21 CFR 133" is a 1977 numbering, so it could not have been "entered" in 1950. The page paraphrases rather than quotes 133.182, so "verbatim" is overstated.

why: The regulation says "not less than 35 °F", i.e. 35 °F or warmer, not strictly "above". "Federal" added because the rule lives in the FDA standards of identity (and the interstate raw-milk ban, 21 CFR 1240.61). The zh「35°F 以上」already reads as inclusive and needs no change.

new: 联邦标准（21 CFR 133.165）规定用牛奶、含水不超过 32%、固形物中乳脂不少于 32%、熟成至少 10 个月，还写了基本做法，只是不限产地。联盟给美国门店的指南明确说不能写
why: 133.165 不只要求牛奶和 10 个月：还规定含水 ≤32%、固形物乳脂 ≥32%，并在 (b) 段写明了做法（加乳酸菌、凝乳酶，切到麦粒大小，加热到 115–125°F，入模、压、盐渍、熟成），所以「做法不限」不对；真正不限的是产地。联盟的美国指南本身声明不具法律约束力，用「指南明确说不能」比「规定」更准（指南原话是 NOT ALLOWED）。

old: 硬质、半硬奶酪把霉点四周和下方约 1 英寸（2.5 厘米）切掉，其余可吃；软质和新鲜奶酪一旦长了不该有的霉，整块扔掉。
new: 硬质、半硬奶酪把霉点四周和下方至少 1 英寸（2.5 厘米）切掉，刀别碰到霉，切完换新纸包好，其余可吃；软质和新鲜奶酪，以及刨丝、切片、弄碎的奶酪（不论哪种），一旦长了不该有的霉，整块扔掉。
why: USDA FSIS 的说法是「至少」1 英寸、刀不要碰到霉以免带到别处，并且刨丝、切片、碎奶酪（任何种类）长霉一律扔掉——原文漏了这一条，读者可能把长霉的硬质奶酪丝也切一切接着吃。

confirmed: 60-day rule: 'not less than 35 °F for not less than 60 days' for unpasteurized milk confirmed verbatim in 21 CFR 133.182(a); fresh raw-milk cheese cannot be sold at US counters in practice (federal standards + 21 CFR 1240.61 interstate ban). Zh THESIS「35°F 以上」fine. Origin year: use 'traces to 1949' (final rule published 22 Apr 1949 per Knoll 2005); 1950 is a secondary-source date. The 13 Oct 2026 amendment to Part 133 (91 FR 65059) is the salt-substitutes rule and does not touch the 60-day requirement.
21 CFR 133.182 'made from ___' milk labelling confirmed (para. e); 21 CFR 133.165 and 133.169 cited sections exist and say what is described, apart from the fixes listed.

Gruyère: TTAB found GRUYERE generic; E.D. Va. (Judge Ellis) granted summary judgment in 2021 (575 F. Supp. 3d 627); Fourth Circuit affirmed 3 Mar 2023 (No. 22-1041). Opposers USDEC, Atalanta, Intercibus; court relied on FDA standard 21 CFR 133.149 (no geography) and gruyere made in Germany, Wisconsin (Emmi Roth) and Idaho (Glanbia, Blackfoot). hist_A gruyere entry and counter_D swiss-aop text are correct.
Swiss Gruyère: AOC 2001, AOP from 2013. French Gruyère is an EU PGI (Reg. (EU) No 110/2013), with holes and a mandatory 'France' indication (wording clarified above).

Parmigiano Reggiano: pin-dot band carries PARMIGIANO-REGGIANO, dairy number, month/year and DOP (FAQ); Mezzano = parallel grooves, second grade, eat young; age bands 12–19 / 20–26 / 27–34 / 35–45 months; Export = first grade checked at 18 months, Premium = checked at 24 months plus sensory score, Prodotto di montagna = mountain area, checked at 20 months; grated PR may not contain anti-caking agents or cellulose; 'naturally lactose-free' is in the Consortium FAQ and US guidelines (but the parm-lactose label is not shown on the page).
